cur:objects-coin-john-i-tzimiskes-histam.summary: The obverse presents the bust of Christ Pantokrator, blessing and holding the Gospels, in a cross-nimbus. On the reverse the Virgin Mary, with the hand of God above, joins the emperor John I Tzimiskes in holding a patriarchal cross, a sign that his rule is sanctioned from heaven. Christ above, his Mother interceding: the coin is a compact statement of Byzantine political theology.
facts: This issue continues the scheme, revived after Iconoclasm, of Christ on the obverse and the ruler on the reverse, which remained the norm of Byzantine gold coinage until the end of the Empire (Wikipedia, Byzantine coinage).

cur:objects-coin-john-i-tzimiskes-histam.notes: John I is traditionally credited (after the chronicler Skylitzes) with introducing the anonymous folles bearing Christ's image; this attribution is not certain and is not used as a fact here.

vam:O1028904.summary: Inside a large blue initial A, the risen Christ, with a golden halo and a pale mantle, stands above the closed tomb against a blue sky, his right hand raised in blessing and his left holding a cross-staff with the banner of the Resurrection. Around the initial, staves of square music notation and Gothic script carry the chant, framed by a border of coiling stems, flowers and gold sprays. The leaf comes from a choir book and opens the chant for the Easter vigil, so the image greeted the singers at the first Alleluia of Easter.
facts: The red rubric explains that the antiphon was sung in choir on the vigil of Easter after the priest's communion at Mass, followed by the music for 'Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia'.
An inscription on the leaf records its purchase from Selb in Cologne in 1857; it was transferred from the Art Museum in December 1863.
vam:O1028904.notes: Worklist year (850) was an error: the V&A dates the leaf to the third quarter of the 15th century (Germany, probably Cologne). The V&A record (museum no. 3077) gives no medium; the usual technique would be ink, tempera and gold on parchment, but this has not been recorded here.
